placements.why: The envelope's entire content is a calibration verification record (instrument, calibration value, verification method, result). The org's named taxonomy of top-level strata categories explicitly includes 'Calibration' as a canonical top-level name, but this repo's EXISTING STRATA is empty — nothing has been minted here yet. This content is an exact, unambiguous instance of that category, so it mints the strata node verbatim from the taxonomy rather than inventing a paraphrase or forcing the content under an unrelated category.
placements.title: instrument calibration and verification work as its own organizational category
placements.frame: What instrument, standard, or process is being calibrated or verified here, and does the record show the calibration holding?
consulted: org taxonomy list in pass instructions: Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Architecture/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration

placements.title: an instrument's calibration moves from unverified to checked-and-holding against a reference standard
placements.frame: Has this instrument's calibration been checked against a named reference standard, and does the record show it holding across the relevant range?
placements.why: src-1 states the Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration at 88.4 MHz was verified against the June reference plates and holds across the full observing band; src-2 and src-3 restate the same event in structured field form (instrument name, calibration value + verification basis). Per the grain test, the specific 88.4 MHz figure and the June-plates check are facts/evidence, not a leaf themselves — but 'instrument calibration gets checked against a reference standard and confirmed to hold' is a subject future calibration envelopes (other instruments, other reference sets, re-checks) will keep feeding, so it earns a thematic leaf under the newly-minted Calibration strata rather than being left as a bare fact. The existing graph structure was empty, so nothing could be reused; this names the leaf the content itself calls for.
